stemMd: A homologous chromosome pair fails to separate in meiosis I, but meiosis II proceeds normally. Considering only that pair, what four gamete types result?

options.label: A
options.textMd: Two with an extra chromosome and two missing that chromosome

options.label: C
options.textMd: One with an extra chromosome and three normal

options.label: E
options.textMd: Two normal and two with extra chromosomes

explanationMd: Both homologues enter one meiosis-I daughter and neither enters the other. After normal sister-chromatid separation, two gametes carry both homologues and two carry neither, yielding n+1 and n−1 classes.

distractorRationale.d: The first-division error affects both daughter lineages.
distractorRationale.e: The complementary missing-chromosome gametes are omitted.
distractorRationale.c: This is not the outcome of a first-division failure.
distractorRationale.b: Only one homologous pair failed to segregate.
